newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, seen treading water.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, seen treading water.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased on Friday to end the week one percent down on profit-taking traders said and predicted the index would track sideways in the medium term.

"I believe this week some investors wanted to cash in the profits after last week's jump while others wanted to bring prices down by selling in order to be able to buy at lower prices later," one trader said.

He said the index would drift over the next two weeks but could start rising again in the second half of August when brokers start to prepare for an expected revival of investment activities in September.
"In the past couple of years September was usually quite hot on the Ljubljana bourse so everyone expects that it will be so this year, too," an analyst said.
The SBI index slipped 1.51 points or 0.1 pct to 1,552.66.
Overall seven shares fell, nine rose, four were uchanged and eight were untraded. Turnover rose to 267.6 billion tolars from 125.7 billion.

Analysts attributed the strong turnover to profit-taking in petrol trader Petrol. Petrol was the most actively traded share, down 1.49 percent to 24,500 tolars on volume of 6,527 shares for total turnover of 159.5 million tolars.
Financial consultancy Primofin led decliners, down 14.29 percent to 9,000 on volume of only eight shares. Analysts said poor liquidity was seen as the sole reason for the fall.

Health resort Terme Catez was the biggest gainer, up 3.28 percent to 12,600 on volume of 46 shares, rebounding after a four percent fall in the past three days. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
